Apple - Apple Scab.description: Apple scab is a fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis. It appears as dark, velvety spots on leaves and fruits, reducing yield and marketability.
symptoms: Dark olive-green to brown spots on leaves
causes: Thrives in cool, wet spring conditions
prevention: Prune trees for better air circulation
treatment: Apply fungicides (captan, myclobutanil) at bud break
Repeat every 7-14 days during wet periods
Use copper-based sprays as organic alternative

Apple - Black Rot.description: Black rot is a fungal disease caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa, affecting leaves, fruit, and bark of apple trees.
symptoms: Brown sunken lesions on fruit turning black
prevention: Remove mummified fruits and dead wood
treatment: Maintain tree health through proper fertilization

Apple - Healthy.description: This apple plant appears healthy with no signs of disease. Continue regular monitoring and preventive care.
prevention: Monitor regularly for early signs of disease

Corn - Common Rust.description: Common rust is a fungal disease caused by Puccinia sorghi, one of the most widespread diseases of corn worldwide.
symptoms: Small, golden-brown to dark brown pustules on leaves
Pustules appear on both leaf surfaces
Severe infection causes yellowing and death of leaves
prevention: Early planting to avoid peak infection periods
treatment: Apply fungicides (triazoles, strobilurins) at early infection
Most economic loss prevention comes from resistant varieties

Corn - Healthy.description: This corn plant is healthy. Maintain good cultural practices to keep plants disease-free throughout the season.

Grape - Black Rot.description: Grape black rot, caused by Guignardia bidwellii, is one of the most destructive diseases of cultivated grapes in warm, humid areas.
symptoms: Brown circular lesions with dark borders on leaves
Infected berries turn brown then black and mummify
causes: Overwinters in mummified berries and canes
Wet weather during bloom is critical infection period
prevention: Remove mummified berries and infected canes in winter
Ensure good canopy ventilation through pruning
treatment: Apply fungicides (myclobutanil, mancozeb) starting at bud break
Continue spray program every 10-14 days through fruit set

Grape - Healthy.description: This grape vine is healthy. Proper canopy management and preventive sprays will keep it productive.
prevention: Preventive fungicide sprays during wet springs

Potato - Early Blight.description: Early blight, caused by Alternaria solani, is a common fungal disease affecting potato leaves, stems, and tubers.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target-board pattern)
Lesions start on lower, older leaves
causes: Favored by warm days (75-85°F), cool nights
Stress from drought, nutrient deficiency increases susceptibility
treatment: Begin sprays when first symptoms appear

Potato - Late Blight.description: Late blight, caused by Phytophthora infestans, is one of the most devastating plant diseases in history (responsible for the Irish Potato Famine).
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves turning dark brown to black
White mold on underside of leaves in humid conditions
Rapid collapse of entire plant in severe outbreaks
causes: Spreads rapidly; can destroy entire crop in days
prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation; water in morning
treatment: Destroy severely infected crops to prevent spread

Potato - Healthy.description: This potato plant is healthy. Monitor regularly as potatoes are susceptible to several serious diseases.

Tomato - Bacterial Spot.description: Bacterial spot is caused by Xanthomonas species and affects leaves, stems, and fruit of tomato plants.
symptoms: Small, water-soaked lesions on leaves turning dark brown
Raised, rough, scabby spots on fruit
causes: Bacteria: Xanthomonas vesicatoria, X. euvesicatoria, X. gardneri, X. perforans
Spreads via splashing water, contaminated tools
prevention: Rotate crops; avoid working with wet plants
treatment: No cure once infected; manage spread
Remove and destroy severely infected plants

Tomato - Early Blight.description: Tomato early blight (Alternaria solani) causes significant yield losses by reducing the photosynthetic area of the plant.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves
Dark, leathery lesions at stem end of fruit
causes: Survives in soil and infected debris
treatment: Spray every 7-10 days during wet weather

Tomato - Late Blight.description: Tomato late blight (Phytophthora infestans) is the same pathogen that caused the Irish Potato Famine and can devastate entire tomato crops.
symptoms: Pale green to brown water-soaked patches on leaves
White fuzzy growth on undersides in humid conditions
Large, dark, firm lesions on fruit
causes: Thrives in cool (60-70°F), very wet conditions
Spreads extremely rapidly in ideal conditions
prevention: Space plants for good air circulation
treatment: Remove and bag infected plant material immediately

Tomato - Healthy.description: This tomato plant is healthy and thriving. Regular monitoring and good cultural practices will keep it productive.
